title: Engineer career lens 1:1 notes — Camila Torres
content:
Context / purpose:
- Prep for weekly skip-level 1:1 with report (Ravi). Focus = unblock, career coaching, and aligning next quarter priorities. Keep it ~25–30 minutes.
- Tone: curious, coach-first, specific examples, leave space for Ravi to lead on proposals.

Agenda (25 mins):
1) Quick personal check-in (3m) — energy, focus, anything outside work 
2) Wins & signals (5m) — where Ravi felt momentum last week
3) Current blockers & asks (7m) — engineering blockers, infra tickets, staffing
4) Career & scope conversation (7m) — stretch opportunities, mentorship, promotion readiness signals
5) Action items + follow-ups (3m)

Top-of-mind bullets to bring up:
- Noticed Ravi shipped the async batching refactor; perf dashboard shows ~18% lower p99 latency for short sequences (see PR). Flag strong ownership.
- He flagged load-testing failures on Dedicated cluster B during yesterday’s run — need root cause or mitigation.
- Ravi asked for more ownership on rollout policies + canary automation (product asks).

Recent signals / data points:
- PR: platform/pull/479 — batch refactor (author: r.kumar). 4 approvals, QA notes outstanding on error cases.
- Incident log: Dedicated-B-0426 — spike in memory pressure; correlates with heavy prefix cache invalidation.
- Metrics to show during 1:1 if asked: 7-day error budget burn (0.8%), PR throughput (3 PRs merged last sprint), oncall pager count (2 pages last 2 weeks).

Coaching / career focus (goal: promotion to Senior Engineer within next 9–12 months):
- Strengths: deep ownership of infra code, clear PRs, good cross-team communication.
- Growth areas: technical breadth on runtime kernel tuning; mentoring others (has led 1 pairing session — encourage recurring teaching), measurable impact on reliability metrics.
- Concrete suggestions to propose:
  • Lead a small project to add automated canary rollback policy for model-variant mismatches (6–8 weeks).
  • Host a brown-bag on batching strategies and KV cache semantics (target next month).
  • Pair with Obinna on quantization validation tests to broaden arch exposure.

Conversation prompts (open-ended):
- What's the single thing I could remove from your plate to double your focus on the canary project?
- Which kernel/infra area do you want to own next quarter and why?
- Who on the team would you like to mentor — and what's one concrete next step to start?

Blockers to resolve this sprint (expected outcomes):
- Dedicated-B instability: get a postmortem or mitigation plan (owner: infra SRE; ask them to join next sync if needed).
- QA notes on PR 479: request a test sign-off timeline from QA (owner: Ravi to coordinate; due: 2026-04-23).
- Lack of automation for canary rollback: create 3-step proposal + initial spike (owner: Ravi; due: 2026-05-07).

Action items (to confirm in meeting):
- Ravi: post a short RFC draft for canary rollback automation (link in thread). Due: 2026-05-07.
- Me (Camila): connect Ravi with Obinna and the quantization test owner; intro + meeting calendar invite. Due: 2026-04-22.
- Ravi + QA: triage remaining QA comments on PR 479 and list test gaps. Due: 2026-04-23.
- Team: schedule a 60-min brown-bag slot for Ravi (product & infra invited). Target week of 2026-05-03. Owner: Camila to book.

Notes-to-self (during meeting):
- Praise concrete example of shipping (PR 479) early in the check-in.
- If Ravi is uncertain about promotion timing, set expectations: need 2 more cross-team initiatives + evidence of mentoring.
- If he asks for stretch but limited bandwidth, offer to re-prioritize his current non-critical tasks for next 6 weeks.

Open questions / follow-ups to capture:
- Do we have a dedicated perf benchmarking job to measure kernel changes on Dedicated-B variant? (If not, raise with release-eng).
- Who owns long-term prefix-cache resilience work and roadmap? (Possible partnership with serving-runtime.)

Meeting close script (2–3 lines):
- Summarize agreed actions + owners. Ask: "Do any of these feel like the wrong priority?" Confirm calendar invites and who will follow up on what.

Post-meeting quick follow-up template (to send in Slack or email):
- "Thanks for the sync — notes: (1) you’ll draft RFC for canary rollback (due X), (2) I’ll set up intro to Obinna by Y, (3) QA will triage PR 479 by Z. I’ll add these to the team board. Any adjustments?"

Rough backlog / ideas to track (not immediate):
- Automated chaos tests for cache eviction edge cases.
- Quick visualization for canary rollout traffic split history (helps postmortems).
- Small incentive program: pair-hours credit for engineers who mentor 3 junior devs this quarter.

End.
